persona.who: 25, Tamil-Singaporean analyst at a bank, first in family to go to university, got promoted early, feels she doesn't belong in the room.
persona.note: got promoted ahead of people with MBAs. in every meeting I think they're going to find out I'm just the girl from the HDB whose dad drove a taxi. I over prepare for everything and still feel sick before presenting

understanding.bridge: The verdict you keep passing on yourself for not having the right background is what the Gita calls the mind turned into its own enemy.
understanding.week_thesis: This week moves you from the verdict you keep passing on yourself to the one thing you know that no one else in that room knows.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the sick feeling and the replaying, named without judgement.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that it is the verdict, not the background, that makes the room feel dangerous.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what you have built is real and yours.
week_beats.act: You try naming one thing you know before the next meeting, and letting your preparation carry you in.
week_beats.story: A woman who rose from the HDB to lead shows you what standing in your own knowledge looks like.

understanding.core_struggle: She was promoted ahead of people and now believes she is a fraud who will be exposed, despite over-preparing for every presentation.
understanding.mirror: You over-prepare for every meeting, and still feel sick before you walk in.
understanding.insight: It isn't the MBA or the HDB that keeps you sick. It's the verdict you've passed on yourself that your worth was never theirs to grant.

queries.hook: The sick feeling before every presentation, and the replaying of a background that feels like proof you do not belong. I feel like an imposter.
queries.diagnose: When a mind turns against itself, it measures worth by what it lacks and not by what it has done; self-blame grows from believing one background disqualifies a whole life.
queries.steady: Your worth is not theirs to grant; what you have built with your own hands and mind is real, and no one who has earned their place is ever a fraud.
queries.act: Lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down; before the next meeting, name one thing you know that they do not.
queries.story: A woman of humble beginnings who rose to lead, facing a room of doubt and proving that what she built was hers, not theirs to give or take.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on the five causes behind every action.
verse.sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
verse.line: Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.
verse.translation: The seat, the doer, the various instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fifth, providence: these are the five causes of every action.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not 'it wasn't my fault'. You own your part; you just aren't the only cause.

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna about the five roots behind every action. There is the setting, the person acting, the tools they use, the effort they put in, and the unseen hand. You are only one of those five. This means you own your part in what happens, but you do not own the whole outcome.
verse.for_you: When you feel sick before a presentation, you are treating yourself as the only cause of the result. You are carrying the weight of the setting, the tools, the effort, and the unseen, all by yourself. Let the room, the topic, and the audience be the other four causes.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi tells Yudhishthira that a person should never look down on themselves. The one who despises themselves never finds real prosperity. She argues that waiting on fate is no plan, and that effort still matters.
verse.for_you: The verdict you pass on yourself is the real enemy in that room. It is not your background that makes the air feel dangerous. It is the story you tell yourself about not belonging. The text says self-contempt never leads to good. Let that be the pattern you see today.

verse.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verse.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verse.sanskrit: न लोके राजते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया / अपिचेह मृजाहीनः कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते
verse.line: Self-praise never made anyone shine; real ability shows even without polish.
verse.translation: A fool does not shine in the world by praising himself; but a truly accomplished person shines even without polish.
verse.why: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

prasang.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
prasang.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
prasang.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

verse.meaning: The righteous meat-seller tells the proud ascetic that a fool does not shine by praising himself. A truly accomplished person shines even without polish. Real ability shows in honest work, even when it looks ordinary.
verse.for_you: Yesterday you saw the pattern of self-contempt. Today, look at the work you have built. It is real and it is yours. You do not need to polish your background to prove your worth. Your ability shows in the work itself. Hold that.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after he has lost his kingdom. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt or settle for little. She says to set his mind on what is truly good, to stop fearing, and to pull himself together. She does not promise him the kingdom back. She only tells him that his past loss does not define him, and that those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: The presentation is not your kingdom, and no one is trying to take it. You have already built what is in front of you, and that is real and yours. Let your preparation carry you in, and let the room see what you have made.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, at a moment when his mind has been turned inward against him, making him feel small and afraid of his own worth. Krishna says that the self is the only friend a person can truly count on, and the self is also the only enemy that can tear them down. He tells Arjuna to lift himself up by his own mind, and not to let his own thoughts drag him under. The choice is in how Arjuna holds himself, not in the crowd around him.
verse.for_you: Before you open your laptop for the next meeting, name one thing you know. Then let your preparation carry you in. You are the one who has to lift you up, not the background you think you lack.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.for_you: You have already done the work. Let your preparation carry you in, and let the results be what they are. Your part is to show up, and that is enough.

story.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
story.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
story.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
story.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

anchor.speaker: Jambavan
anchor.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
anchor.sanskrit: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
anchor.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
anchor.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
anchor.why: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

story.for_you: You have the strength and the brains to do this work. The promotion was not a mistake. Stop holding yourself back. Step into the room knowing that your part is simply to speak what you know.

script: You are sitting in your apartment, maybe on the edge of your bed, staring at your phone. The promotion is real, but the fear that you are a fraud is loud. You have prepared every slide until your eyes burn. Yet you feel sick. Not because you lack the work.

Arjuna is on a battlefield. He has asked Krishna a long question about what separates action from inaction. Krishna is answering him, standing in his chariot. He is about to tell Arjuna that no one ever acts without help. And he says:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्, विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम्.
In plain words: Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.

Krishna tells Arjuna that every action has five causes. The setting, the doer, the tools, the effort, and the unseen. You are only one of those five. This is hard to accept because the mind wants to claim all the credit for success and all the blame for failure. But you cannot control the mood in the room, the quality of the microphone, or how the audience receives the news. You can only control your part. That is the truth underneath the noise.

Before your next meeting, let the room, the topic, and the people in that chair be the other four causes. You do not have to make the whole thing work. You only have to do your part. Let the setting and the unseen carry the rest.
You are one cause among five.

depth.life: You sit in your chair before the meeting and your body tightens. You rehearse the slides again because you believe if you miss one detail, everyone will see you do not belong there. You are carrying the whole room on your shoulders.
depth.points: You are only one cause among five. The setting, the tools, the effort, and what you cannot see all play their part. When you treat your part as the whole, you turn your mind into its own enemy.
depth.practice: Before your next presentation, name one thing outside yourself that will help it go well, such as the audience or the topic.
depth.question: What would change if you let the room help carry the weight?
